title: iPad (11th gen) charging port cleaning and replacement check
diagnosis: Most often an iPad won't charge because of lint packed in the USB-C port or a worn cable or adapter. I'll have you rule those out first, then clean the port and check that nothing is damaged inside it.
safety_notes: Never use metal pins or needles in the port, as they can short pins or bend contacts.
Unplug the cable before cleaning the port.
Stop and do not charge if the iPad feels hot, or the case looks swollen or bulging.

steps.title: Unplug and power off
steps.instruction: Unplug any cable from the iPad and hold the top button to power it off. Remove any case that covers the bottom edge.
steps.expected_visual_state: The iPad screen is black, no cable is attached, and the bottom edge is uncovered.
common_mistakes: Cleaning the port while a cable is still plugged in
Leaving a thick case on that blocks access to the port

steps.title: Try a different cable and adapter
steps.instruction: Plug a known-good USB-C cable into a different known-good wall adapter, then connect it to the iPad. Leave it for 15 minutes in case the battery is fully drained.
steps.expected_visual_state: The iPad is connected to a cable and wall adapter, and a charging battery icon or lightning bolt may appear on screen.
common_mistakes: Using a computer USB port, which may deliver too little power
Giving up after only a minute with a deeply drained battery

steps.title: Inspect the USB-C port
steps.instruction: Unplug the cable and shine a torch into the USB-C port on the bottom edge. Look for lint, dirt or bent contacts.
steps.expected_visual_state: The phone camera sees the iPad bottom edge with a light shining into the port, showing the central tongue and any debris.
common_mistakes: Not using enough light to see the lint
Mistaking the central tongue for damage

steps.title: Clean out the port
steps.instruction: Gently scrape along the inside walls of the port with a wooden toothpick to lift out lint. Do not press on the central tongue.
steps.expected_visual_state: A toothpick is in the port and small pieces of lint are visible on its tip or on the table.
common_mistakes: Using a metal pin that can short or bend contacts
Pushing lint deeper instead of lifting it out
Pressing hard on the central tongue

steps.title: Re-inspect the port
steps.instruction: Shine the torch in again to check the port is clean and the contacts look straight. Blow out any dust with a short puff of air.
steps.expected_visual_state: The port interior looks clean with a straight central tongue and no visible debris.
common_mistakes: Using compressed air cans at close range, which can push in moisture
Missing remaining lint at the very back of the port

steps.title: Test charging
steps.instruction: Plug in the known-good cable and adapter firmly, then wait a couple of minutes. Check that the charging icon appears and the battery percentage rises.
steps.expected_visual_state: The iPad screen shows a charging lightning bolt on the battery icon, or the percentage is climbing.
common_mistakes: Not pushing the cable in fully so it clicks into place
Expecting an instant response from a very low battery
